title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a hand-corrected typescript (numbered 18) of what became SGA 6, Exposé X, §7, on specialization of cycles and K-theory. It seems misfiled in the 'Motifs et théorie de Hodge' folder. Evidence: the numbering 7.13.x, the internal references (XIV 4.1), (SGA 5 IV) and (7.14), and the use of Gr^i, the graded pieces of K-theory for the topological filtration.

Setting: f: X → S is proper, later assumed smooth and proper. t is a point specializing to s, with geometric points t̄ and s̄.

Diagram (7.13.10) states that two maps commute: the specialization map Gr^i(X_t̄)_Q → Gr^i(X_s̄)_Q on rational graded K-groups, and the ℓ-adic cycle class map cl into H^{2i}(-, Q_ℓ(i)). The right vertical arrow is the cospecialization isomorphism of smooth proper base change.

Remark 7.13.11 comments on this and on the preceding diagram (7.13.9):
- The compatibility 'specialization of algebraic cycles is compatible with ℓ-adic cycle classes' is unsatisfactory because it is only proved rationally, so torsion is lost.
- A torsion-sensitive statement would need the Chow ring. There the cycle class is naturally defined as a map CH^* → H^{2*}(-, Z_ℓ(*)) (compare XIV 4.1). On Gr^* of K-theory, by contrast, one only gets a comparison up to torsion: Gr^i ⊗ Q ≅ CH^i ⊗ Q.
- But no specialization theory for Chow rings existed yet (cf. 7.14).
- What can be said, for f smooth and proper, is diagram (7.13.12). Here Z^i means cycles of codimension i not modulo any equivalence. Specialization σ sends Z_t to Z_s, where Z is (presumably) the closure of Z_t in X over a trait. With Z_ℓ coefficients, cl∘σ agrees with cl after identifying cohomologies via the specialization/cospecialization isomorphism.

The page ends mid-sentence ('où Z est ...'), presumably continuing 'the schematic closure'.

What the passage serves: compatibility of the SGA 6 intersection formalism with étale cycle classes from SGA 4½/SGA 5, and recording the lack of a Chow-level specialization.
errors: No mathematical error. Typo: 'ce trouve' should be 'se trouve'.

Minor: in (7.13.12) the cycles live on X_t and X_s, not on geometric fibres. Implicitly one passes to cohomology of geometric fibres, or uses a strictly henselian base, to have the base change isomorphism.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft page of published SGA 6 Exp. X 7.13.11. The gap it notes (specialization for Chow rings) was filled by Fulton's theory a few years later. Nothing unpublished of substance.
transcription_corrections: Right vertical arrow in (7.13.12) is drawn as a double-headed arrow (cospecialization isomorphism); the hand-corrected arrowhead points down.
Handwritten insertion reads 'lorsque f : X → S est lisse et propre,'.
The reference originally typed 7.14 was corrected by hand (digit overwritten), likely '7.14'.
